metric_definitions.request_validity: Over every send step of every generated test: the request is replayed through the rules-engine oracle in sequence (same set-up and time steps). A request counts as well-formed if (a) protocol.codec.decode_request decodes it and (b) the oracle does not reject it with a format NRC (0x11 serviceNotSupported, 0x12 subFunctionNotSupported, 0x13 incorrectMessageLengthOrInvalidFormat), unless that NRC is listed in the template's declared intended_nrcs (a deliberate malformed-request probe such as write_did_invalid_length -> 0x13). rate = well-formed / send steps. The unadjusted rate (no intent exemption) is reported alongside.
metric_definitions.expected_response_accuracy: SELF-CONSISTENCY CHECK, circular by construction (expected bytes are produced by the same oracle; reported in an appendix, not a headline). oracle: share of generated send steps whose expected response frames equal a fresh rules-engine re-run of the test (and share of whole tests with zero mismatches). simulator: share of generated tests passing on the bug-free independent simulator. gold: (1) exact overlap = generated tests whose full step sequence (requests and set-up/time steps, ignoring expected responses) is identical to a gold test; agreement = identical expected responses on every step. (2) shared-prefix overlap = every distinct send step reached by an identical step prefix from power-on in both a generated and a gold test (deduplicated by prefix); agreement = identical expected frames for that step.
metric_definitions.coverage: Number of generated tests per category (positive/negative/session/security/timing) per requirement. rate = requirements with >= 1 generated test / requirements; category_presence = categories with >= 1 test across the suite / 5.
metric_definitions.template_reuse_rate: Share of generated tests whose template_id is a registered template AND whose steps are byte-identical to a fresh instantiation of that template with the test's stored parameters (independent re-check of byte provenance).
metric_definitions.citation_validity: Share of all citations attached to generated tests for which rag.citations.citation_is_valid is true against the evaluation corpus (source+ref exists; a quote must appear verbatim and its hex identifiers must belong to the chunk).
metric_definitions.bug_detection_rate: Each catalog bug is enabled alone in a fresh simulator per test. A bug is detected if >= 1 test that passes on the clean simulator fails with the bug enabled. Tests failing on the clean simulator are reported as invalid and get no credit. rate = detected bugs / catalog bugs. Reported for the generated suite, the hand-written gold suite (baseline) and their union. The 26-bug catalog (data/bugs/bug_catalog.yaml) is IN-SAMPLE: templates v2 were added after inspecting which of these bugs v1 missed.
metric_definitions.heldout_bug_detection_rate: Same procedure as bug_detection_rate on the 12 held-out bugs in data/bugs/heldout_catalog.yaml, written by a subagent that could not see templates, gold tests, eval, LLM or agent code. HEADLINE = held-out generated-suite detection. Missed-bug reasons come from a static trigger analysis (eval/heldout.py): whether any test applies the stimulus the bug description needs; reporting only.
metric_definitions.simulator_rules_agreement: A deterministic seeded random sample (eval/agreement.py; >= 5000 requests over 60-step walks with clock advances, environment/DTC changes and computed seed/key handshakes) is sent to a bug-free SimulatedEcu and a RulesSession in lockstep. agreed = requests with byte-identical response frames; a walk stops at its first disagreement.
metric_definitions.udsoncan_virtual_can: udsoncan.Client over ISO-TP on a python-can virtual bus against the simulator: 10 03 -> 27 01 seed -> 27 02 key -> 22 0100 -> 2E 0100 50 -> 22 0100 read-back == 0x50. pass/fail (fail includes any exception, with its text); 'skipped' with --skip-can.
metric_definitions.gold_clean_pass: Gold tests passing on the bug-free simulator / gold tests.
metric_definitions.pipeline_stats: Per requirement: kept tests, dropped tests (failed validation), rejected planner choices, plan attempts (retries = attempts - 1), run status.
metric_definitions.runtime: Wall-clock seconds per evaluation phase and in total (machine dependent).
metric_definitions.target_identification: Label set = target_services U target_dids U target_routines (typed, so service 0x22 and DID 0x0022 differ). Two predicted sets: (a) 'parsed' = services U dids U routines of the ParsedRequirement returned by the pipeline; (b) 'exercised' = every SID of every send step in the requirement's generated tests, every DID named by a 0x22 (all complete pairs) or 0x2E (first pair) request, and every routine id of a 0x31 request. Exact match = predicted set equals label set; for a requirement with an empty label set (NAT-020, unsupported) exact match additionally requires zero generated tests. Micro precision / recall / F1 sum TP / FP / FN over requirements.
metric_definitions.category_recall: |required_categories n categories of the requirement's generated tests| / |required_categories|. Micro = summed numerators / summed denominators; macro = mean over requirements with >= 1 required category (NAT-020 has none and is excluded).
metric_definitions.precondition_recall: |required_preconditions n preconditions established by >= 1 generated test| / |required_preconditions|, `none` skipped (requirements whose label is `none` are excluded). 'Established' is derived statically from each test's concrete steps and oracle-expected responses (mapping below). Micro and macro as for categories.
metric_definitions.fallback: A requirement counts as fallback / produced-nothing if the pipeline status is not 'completed', or the parsed requirement has no services, DIDs or routines, or it kept zero tests. Reported with the list of ids (for NAT-020 producing nothing is the correct outcome).
metric_definitions.heldout_v2_bug_detection_rate: Same procedure as bug_detection_rate on the 15 held-out v2 bugs in data/bugs/heldout_v2_catalog.yaml (heldout_v2: true), written blind after the Part C freeze and SEEN since Part D. Generated-suite detection, where the generated suite is the tests generated from the 15 seed requirements (the same definition as the held-out v1 headline). Supplementary: detection by the union of all generated tests (seed + natural v1 + natural v2) and by the natural-v2 tests alone. Missed-bug reasons come from eval/heldout_v2.py (static trigger predicates written before any v2 result).
metric_definitions.natural_v2_understanding: Requirement understanding on data/requirements_natural_v2.csv (16 rows, split test2, written blind after the freeze) with the same label schema and scoring as the v1 natural set; test2 is the headline split.
metric_definitions.part_d_detection: Per bug catalog and LLM mode: (a) requirement_driven = the tests generated from the 15 seed requirements (exactly the Part C 'generated' suite, comparable with Part C); (b) conformance = the requirement-independent conformance sweep alone (uds_assistant/testgen/conformance.py, generated deterministically from the spec; it uses no LLM and is the same in every mode); (c) full_output = (a) union (b), the system's full output. A bug counts as detected by a suite when a test that passes on the clean simulator fails with the bug enabled; (c) is computed per bug from (a) and (b) because every test runs on a fresh simulator.
metric_definitions.conformance_sweep: Setups (spec-derived states) x stimuli (spec-derived requests and mutations), each followed by a fixed probe set; every expected byte from the rules engine; reduced by deterministic greedy covering. Deterministic lazy-greedy set cover over oracle-observable items, in priority phases; each phase adds tests until its items are covered or the cap is reached, ties broken by catalog order (setup, then stimulus). Phase 1: every (stimulus, response class) the oracle can produce for it over all setups, and every (setup, service family) pair for the spec's services. Phase 2: transition tuples (session, unlocked level, active lockouts, time since last request vs S3, stimulus class, response class) and state effects (stimulus class, response class, which abstract state components changed and how). Phase 3: (stimulus, active session, response class). Phase 4: fine transitions (full abstract pre-state, stimulus class, response class, full abstract post-state).
metric_definitions.heldout_v3_bug_detection: FRESH headline for bugs: the 15 held-out v3 bugs in data/bugs/heldout_v3_catalog.yaml (heldout_v3: true), written blind after the Part D freeze. HEADLINE = detection by the system's FULL OUTPUT = (c) the requirement-driven tests from the 15 seed requirements UNION (per bug) the conformance sweep. Reported next to it and clearly labelled: (a) requirement-driven only (comparable with Part C), (b) the sweep alone, (d) gold. Supplementary: all generated tests (seed + natural v1 + v2 + v3) and the natural-v3 tests alone. Missed-bug reasons come from eval/heldout_v3.py (static trigger predicates written from the bug descriptions before any v3 result existed).
metric_definitions.natural_v3_understanding: Requirement understanding on data/requirements_natural_v3.csv (16 rows, split test3, written blind after the Part D freeze) with the same label schema and scoring as v1 / v2. test3 is the requirement headline. Nothing was tuned on it.
metric_definitions.noise_check: ollama runs the pipeline over natural v3 --noise-runs times in total; run 1 feeds the tables, every run is listed, and the summary is the mean and min-max range over ALL runs (never only the best). mock is deterministic: one run, plus an equality re-run as a check. natural v2 (SEEN) keeps its single run.
metric_definitions.by_kind: Parsed (and exercised) false positives and false negatives by identifier kind (service / did / routine / dtc), per requirement set, from each requirement's missed and extra identifiers. tp = label items of that kind minus the missed ones.
metric_definitions.rejected_by_reason: Rejected planner choices by reason: unknown template id; option index out of range; option not in the offered shortlist; duplicate / other (a choice that previously failed, or an instantiate / validate failure). Counted per requirement set.
metric_definitions.seen_sets: SEEN = their results were known when Part D was designed or tuned: held-out v1 and v2 bugs, natural v1 (test and dev) and v2 requirements. The 26 in-sample bugs were tuned on. Only the v3 rows are independent evidence.

stats.method: Deterministic lazy-greedy set cover over oracle-observable items, in priority phases; each phase adds tests until its items are covered or the cap is reached, ties broken by catalog order (setup, then stimulus). Phase 1: every (stimulus, response class) the oracle can produce for it over all setups, and every (setup, service family) pair for the spec's services. Phase 2: transition tuples (session, unlocked level, active lockouts, time since last request vs S3, stimulus class, response class) and state effects (stimulus class, response class, which abstract state components changed and how). Phase 3: (stimulus, active session, response class). Phase 4: fine transitions (full abstract pre-state, stimulus class, response class, full abstract post-state).

interpretation.text:
### Summary (Part D, fresh v3 data)

All numbers come from one run of `python -m uds_assistant.eval.run_eval --mode ollama --noise-runs 3 --before-after` (mock and the local Qwen2.5-3B model on the same inputs). The v3 sets are fresh: 15 bugs and 16 requirements, each written blind by a subagent after the Part D freeze. Nothing was changed after their results were seen, and every freeze hash still matches. The v1 and v2 sets are seen and appear only as context.

1. **Bug detection on fresh bugs went up, and almost all of the gain comes from the conformance sweep.** The system's full output (requirement-driven tests plus the sweep) catches 10/15 (66.7%) with mock and 9/15 (60.0%) with ollama. The requirement-driven tests alone catch 4/15 (mock) and 2/15 (ollama), the sweep alone 9/15 in both modes, and the gold tests 3/15. The Part C headline on v2 was 2/15, but that was a different bug set, so it is a reference point and not a before/after pair.
2. **The sweep does not depend on the model, and it is cheap.** 1200 tests, generated from the spec in about 7 s, all 1200 pass on the clean simulator, and the bug matrix over all four catalogs took 85 s. It caught 9/15 on seen v2 and 9/15 on fresh v3, so the rate did not drop on bugs written after the freeze.
3. **The model still adds little to bug detection.** With the sweep included, mock is one bug ahead of ollama (10 against 9). The extra bug is `dtc_clear_single_clears_neighbour`, which only the mock's larger requirement-driven suite catches.
4. **Requirement understanding on fresh v3 is better with the model than with the mock, as in Part C, but precision is still poor.** Parsed P/R/F1 is 0.596/0.622/0.609 for ollama and 0.857/0.267/0.407 for mock; category recall is 70.0% against 42.0% and precondition recall 89.7% against 48.3%. Exact parsed match is 2/16 against 1/16. Ollama has 19 false positives (service 15, DID 4) and 17 false negatives (service 9, DID 5, routine 3).
5. **Rejected planner choices went to zero.** Ollama had 15 rejections on the 35 old requirements and 12 on v2 in Part C. It now has 0 on every set, including fresh v3. The likely cause is constrained decoding (the planner can only emit offered options); no ablation was run to confirm it.

### Held-out v3 bug detection (15 bugs, fresh): the headline

| Suite | mock | ollama |
|---|---|---|
| **Full output (requirement-driven + sweep)** | **10/15 (66.7%)** | **9/15 (60.0%)** |
| (a) requirement-driven only (the Part C "generated" suite) | 4/15 (26.7%) | 2/15 (13.3%) |
| (b) conformance sweep alone | 9/15 (60.0%) | 9/15 (60.0%) |
| Gold | 3/15 (20.0%) | 3/15 (20.0%) |
| Tests (requirement-driven / sweep / full) | 206 / 1200 / 1406 | 73 / 1200 / 1273 |

- **Missed by the full output (5 bugs with mock, 6 with ollama).** For each, no test applies the stimulus.
  - `session_switch_keeps_pending_seed`: no test requests a seed, switches session with a positive `10 xx`, then sends a key for that level.
  - `lockout_expiry_resets_attempt_count`: no test reaches a lockout, waits for the delay to expire, requests a seed and sends another wrong key.
  - `nrc_order_subfunction_before_length`: no test sends `10`, `11` or `3E` with an unsupported sub-function and a wrong total length.
  - `read_did_speed_not_clamped`: no test reads DID 0x0140 while the vehicle speed is above 255 kph.
  - `dtc_read_reports_masked_status`: no test reads DTCs where a listed DTC has status bits outside the request mask.
  - ollama only: `dtc_clear_single_clears_neighbour` (no test clears one DTC while the next one is stored and reads back with a mask that shows it).
- **Found by the sweep and not by the requirement-driven tests (6 bugs with mock, 7 with ollama).** For example `failed_key_keeps_pending_seed`, `nrc_order_write_range_before_condition`, `routine_results_trailing_bytes_accepted`, `write_stores_value_before_range_rejection`, `s3_timeout_clears_dtc_status`, `suppressed_request_does_not_restart_s3`. The seed requirements never ask for these stimuli; the sweep applies them without being asked.
- **Gold is lowest (3/15).** The hand-written gold set was written before any v3 bug existed and covers the seed requirements, not systematic state and mutation probing.
- **Caveats.** 15 bugs: one bug is 6.7 points, so a one-bug difference between modes is not evidence of a difference. The bugs were written by a language model. The sweep's expected bytes come from the rules engine, which is also what the simulator is checked against, so a shared misreading would be invisible to both.

### Requirement understanding on natural v3 (16 requirements, fresh): the headline

| Metric | mock | ollama (run 1) | ollama mean over 3 runs (min-max) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parsed exact | 1/16 | 2/16 | - |
| Parsed P / R / F1 | 0.857 / 0.267 / 0.407 | 0.596 / 0.622 / 0.609 | 0.596 / 0.622 / 0.609 (identical) |
| Exercised F1 | 0.342 | 0.472 | 0.465 (0.462-0.472) |
| Category recall (micro) | 42.0% | 70.0% | 70.0% (70.0%-70.0%) |
| Precondition recall (micro) | 48.3% | 89.7% | 89.7% (89.7%-89.7%) |
| Fallback / nothing generated | 7 | 0 | - |

- **Where the model helps.** It finds far more targets than the mock (recall 0.622 against 0.267) and covers more required categories and preconditions. The mock's keyword rules produced nothing for 7 of 16 requirements. The mock again rarely invents a target (2 false positives), but finds about a quarter of them.
- **Precision is still the weak point.** 0.596 on fresh v3, against 0.565 on v2 in Part C. These are different sets, so this is not a measured improvement. The service-evidence grounding did cut false positives on the seen sets (v2 from 30 to 9, v1 test split from 21 to 9), but on fresh v3 the model still adds 15 services (5 times `0x10`, 5 times `0x27`, 2 times `0x2E` and `0x22`, once `0x11`) and 4 DIDs. The Part D changes were designed after reading the earlier false positives, so the fresh number is the honest one.
- **Recall is lower than Part C's v2 run** (0.622 against 0.796). The sets differ, so this may just be set difficulty (v3 avoids the spec's field names). `0x3E` is missed in 2 requirements (NAT3-011, NAT3-012), and the routine id and `0x31` in NAT3-006.
- **Ambiguous rows.** Both ambiguous requirements (NAT3-014, NAT3-015) are partly missed. NAT3-016 (the unsupported feature, no targets) still produces 8 tests and a spurious `0x22`.
- **Noise.** Parsed numbers, category recall and precondition recall were identical in all three runs. Exercised F1 varied by 0.01 (0.462-0.472). Three runs is a small sample.

### Seen sets (context only)

- Natural v2 (seen): ollama parsed P/R/F1 went from 0.565/0.796/0.661 to 0.808/0.775/0.792; precondition recall from 77.8% to 92.6%; category recall from 74.0% to 72.0%. Mock unchanged. The fixes targeted exactly these false positives, so this is not evidence.
- Held-out v1 (seen): full output 12/12 (mock) and 11/12 (ollama). Held-out v2 (seen): full output 9/15 in both modes (Part C: 2/15). In-sample: 26/26 in both modes.
- Latency: ollama mean 21.8 s per requirement over the 35 old ones (21.4 s before), 0.97 explain calls per requirement. Whole evaluation 2327.6 s (about 39 min): ollama 2125.8 s, sweep 100.9 s, mock 73.0 s.

### Provenance, errors, freeze

- Byte provenance passed on every generated test in all runs (mock 613/613, ollama 552/552, sweep 1200/1200): no model-written byte reached any test. This does not show the bytes are right, only where they came from.
- Ollama: 0 truncation events and 0 fallbacks to the mock model. 123 fallback events were all the batched explain step omitting some test ids, so a deterministic explanation was used. They do not affect any score.
- Every Part D freeze hash matches and the frozen paths are clean.

### What would help next

1. Close the five stimuli still missed (seed, session switch, then key; lockout expiry then another wrong key; unsupported sub-function with wrong length; DID read above 255 kph; DTC mask with extra status bits). They are known now, so any template built from them makes v3 seen, and a v4 blind set is needed to measure it.
2. Service precision on fresh phrasing: the model still adds `0x10`/`0x27` where the text does not state them, and still misses `0x3E` in some requirements.
3. Test a larger model or context. Only one 3B model on a 4 GB GPU was tried.
